thread.title_full: Wilmington's Penn Cinema losing theaters in downsize for indoor golf - NewsBreak

author: Ryan Cormier
title: Wilmington's Penn Cinema losing theaters in downsize for indoor golf - NewsBreak
text:
By Ryan Cormier ,
19 hours ago Wilmington's independently owned and operated Penn Cinema Riverfront 14 + IMAX may have the biggest movie screen in Delaware, but the cineplex is about to get smaller.
The multiplex will shrink from 12 screens down to 10, while retaining its showcase IMAX theater. (Penn Cinema also houses three additional theaters, but they have not been in use since the COVID-19 pandemic.)
The ownership of Penn Cinema ‚Äì namesake Penn Ketchum, Pennsylvania-based Byler Holdings LLC and Wilmington developers Buccini Pollin Group ‚Äì is leasing the space to The Clubhouse of Delaware , a new indoor golf facility with golf simulators.
Construction will begin in the spring and The Clubhouse is expected to open by the end of the summer, officials said.
Ketchum said losing two screens will not impact the number of showings of blockbusters and other popular titles.
"What we are moving away from is some of the smaller titles," he said, pointing to Wilmington's pair of art-house theaters, Theatre N and The Screening Room at 1313 , as places where those films will still have a home in the city.
Overall, he sees the diversified entertainment offerings at the property with The Clubhouse as a win-win for both businesses.
After all, the fastest-growing sector of the golf industry is indoor golf, with more people playing indoors nationally than on traditional outdoor golf courses in recent years.
"It's a huge benefit for us: a rising tide lifts all boats. It's a great complement and we'll help each other," said Ketchum, whose Riverfront theater draws about 150,000 theatergoers each year.
Why remove screens? Penn Cinema (401 S. Madison St.) opened in December 2012, seeing space in the market for a state-of-the-art city-based IMAX theater and multiplex located between closest competitors Brandywine Hundred's 16-theater Regal Cinema and the Newport-area 10-screen Cinemark theater.
But two years after Penn Cinema's debut, the 12-screen Cinemark Christiana opened near the Christiana Mall, bringing movies back to the mall for the first time since the closing of the in-mall General Cinemas in the early 2000s after a 20-plus-year run.
The theater also boasts an XD theater with an IMAX-style super-sized screen, although not as large as the IMAX format.
The addition of Cinemark Christiana to the market put a strain on Penn Cinema.
"If they were open when we designed our building, we still would have opened, but we would have opened smaller," Ketchum said.
The future of Penn Cinema on the Riverfront In fact, the downsizing at Penn Cinema may not be over.
Ketchum said he believes the ideal size for the theater is eight screens, including IMAX. That means two more theaters could be converted.
Ownership is currently looking at possibly leasing the space to another business that would fit in the entertainment complex, but Ketchum said no plans have been locked in.
"It would be misleading of me to suggest any of the different ideas where exploring," he said.
Ketchum said there may be changes coming to Penn Cinema's lobby in the future, as well. His Lititz, Pennsylvania, theater installed a self-service beer wall and a full-service bar last year.
"We certainly need to take a second look at that lobby," he said, not committing to a Lititz-style bar makeover. "We love that theater, and we're committed to spending some money to keep it up to date."
What to expect from The Clubhouse The Clubhouse of Delaware is the brainchild of a trio of Delaware friends, golfers and now business partners: Matt Piecara, Rick Knight and Enrico Giancroce.
Piecara, who will be director of golf operations at The Clubhouse, and Knight both recently sold their businesses ‚Äì waste management and landscaping, respectively. Giancroce works in real estate and catering and will be in charge of the food offerings at The Clubhouse.
They said they want their golf facility to be a destination both for families looking for fun and golfers of different skill levels looking to work on their game.
There will be nine bays outfitted with AI-driven GOLFJOY simulators, allowing customers to play any of 400 or so golf courses from around the world, including famous spots such as Scotland's St. Andrews Golf Club and California's Pebble Beach Golf Links. The system measures up to 33 real-time ball and club metrics.
The 8,000-square-foot venue will allow guests to practice, play and even compete in leagues with 3D visuals in 4K definition. A smart putting platform will be included at every simulator, replicating natural green undulations over a 4-yard span for a true-to-life experience, officials said.

The Clubhouse also plans to offer golf lessons and youth programming, joining other upstate indoor golf facilities such as The Back Nine Golf in Brandywine Hundred and Creek Links in Pike Creek.
Piecara, currently enrolled in the PGA Golf Management University Program to obtain PGA professional certification, said the trio has been working on the project for 2¬Ω years.
They nearly opened at The Grove in Newark before settling on the Penn Cinemas location: "It was kind of a no-brainer. This is a better location and gives us more space."
